extracted.intended_audience: teachers, education leaders, curriculum developers, administrators, and policymakers involved in K–12 mathematics education
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive set of principles and standards describing what students should know and be able to do in mathematics from prekindergarten through grade 12 and how schools should organize curriculum, instruction, assessment, teacher preparation, and use of technology to achieve those goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence in mathematics education requires equity—high expectations and strong support for all students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All students, regardless of personal characteristics, backgrounds, or physical challenges, can learn mathematics when they have access to high-quality instruction. Equity does not mean identical instruction for everyone; it requires reasonable and appropriate accommodations and appropriately challenging content to promote access and attainment for all students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: A curriculum is more than a collection of activities; it must be coherent, focused on important mathematics, and well articulated across the grades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a coherent curriculum mathematical ideas are linked and build on one another so students' understanding deepens and their ability to apply mathematics expands. An effective curriculum focuses on important mathematics preparing students for continued study and real-world problem solving, and it challenges students to learn increasingly sophisticated ideas across grade bands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective mathematics teaching requires understanding what students know and need to learn and then challenging and supporting them to learn it well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers must be committed to students as learners, know the mathematics they teach deeply, and be able to draw on that knowledge flexibly. Teachers need ample opportunities and resources for professional growth and support to enhance and refresh their knowledge so they can shape students' understanding, problem-solving ability, and confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must learn mathematics with understanding, actively building new knowledge from experience and previous knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize conceptual understanding aligned with factual knowledge and procedural proficiency. Students should reflect on their thinking, learn from mistakes, develop persistence and curiosity, and gain confidence to tackle difficult tasks. Instruction should promote application and transfer of strategies to other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment should support the learning of important mathematics and furnish useful information to both teachers and students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should be integral to instruction, informing teachers' instructional decisions and conveying to students what kinds of mathematical knowledge and performance are valued. Assessment feedback helps students set goals, assume responsibility for learning, and become more independent learners. Task selection for assessment matters because it signals valued outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology is essential in teaching and learning mathematics; it influences the mathematics that is taught and enhances students' learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate use of technology deepens understanding, supports investigation across content areas, and allows students to focus on decision making, reasoning, reflection, and problem solving. The power and versatility of technology require reconsideration of what mathematics should be taught and how.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and Operations (Content Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deals with understanding numbers, developing meanings of operations, and computing fluently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Young children focus on whole numbers, counting, comparing quantities, and base-ten structure; higher grades emphasize fractions and integers. Students should perform computations in different ways (mental methods, estimations, paper-and-pencil), be able to explain their methods, recognize multiple methods exist, and value methods that are efficient, accurate, and general. Computational fluency helps students make appropriate use of calculators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebra (Content Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic symbols and procedures are critical and are best learned as concepts and techniques tied to representing quantitative relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebra should be taught as a style of mathematical thinking for formalizing patterns, functions, and generalizations; connections to number and real-world situations should be emphasized. Even young children can be encouraged to use algebraic reasoning in exploring patterns and relations; later grade bands extend connections to geometric ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry (Content Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls on students to analyze characteristics of geometric shapes, make mathematical arguments about geometric relationships, and use visualization and geometric modeling to solve problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometry is a setting for developing reasoning and justification skills. Expectations include analyzing shapes, constructing mathematical arguments (not only proofs in the classical sense), using spatial reasoning, and applying geometric modeling to real problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement (Content Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes understanding attributes, units, systems, and processes of measurement and applying techniques, tools, and formulas to determine measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement serves to integrate different strands of mathematics (number, geometry, functions, statistics) by offering opportunities to learn and apply concepts across areas; emphasis is on practical applications and correct use of units and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Analysis and Probability (Content Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls for students to formulate questions and collect, organize, and display relevant data to answer them, and to learn statistical methods and probability concepts for making inferences and predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning statistically is essential for informed citizenship and consumer decisions. Students should learn to analyze data appropriately, make inferences, and understand basic probability concepts in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Solving (Process Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solving problems is both a goal and a major means of learning mathematics; it is integral to the mathematics program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students require frequent opportunities to formulate and solve complex problems requiring significant effort. They should reflect on their thinking during problem solving to adapt strategies to new contexts, thereby acquiring habits of persistence, curiosity, and transferable problem-solving approaches useful beyond mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning and Proof (Process Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical reasoning and proof are powerful ways of developing and expressing insights and justifications about phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should note patterns and structure, ask whether patterns are incidental or explainable, make and investigate conjectures, and develop and evaluate mathematical arguments. Reasoning and proof (with sophistication appropriate to grade level) should be used across content areas so students understand that mathematics makes sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication (Process Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical communication is a way of sharing ideas and clarifying understanding; students should communicate results orally and in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through communicating their thinking students learn to be clear, convincing, and precise in mathematical language. Explanations should include mathematical arguments and rationales, not just procedural descriptions; listening and discussion help learners refine thinking and make connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connections (Process Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics is an integrated field; students should connect mathematical ideas to deepen understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should emphasize interrelatedness of mathematical topics, contexts linking mathematics to other subjects and students' experiences, and help students view mathematics as a coherent whole, thereby enhancing retention and utility of mathematical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations (Process Standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical ideas can be represented in many ways (pictures, concrete materials, tables, graphs, symbols, spreadsheets); representation is fundamental to understanding and using ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should gain access to varied representations and learn to create representations that capture concepts or relationships, expanding their capacity to model and interpret phenomena. Representations reflect cultural refinement and serve as tools for thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and Expectations by Grade Band
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards are revisited and expectations are specified for four grade bands: prekindergarten–grade 2, grades 3–5, grades 6–8, and grades 9–12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content Standards should receive different emphases across grade bands; the document includes an appendix 'Table of Standards and Expectations' detailing grade-band expectations and provides examples and illustrations for each band to guide curriculum, instruction, and assessment alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning with Understanding (Classroom Vision)
rubrics_metrics.description: A vision of classrooms and systems where all students access high-quality, engaging mathematics instruction with ambitious expectations, appropriate accommodations, knowledgeable teachers, rich curriculum, and essential technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students engage in complex tasks chosen carefully, draw on multiple mathematical topics and representations, make and test conjectures with teacher guidance, use varied reasoning and proof techniques, work productively alone or in groups with technology, reflect on progress, and communicate ideas orally and in writing. The vision emphasizes flexibility, resourcefulness, persistence, and valuing mathematics.
